inventory.anchor: include of StealthLoadInfo.h; TRRLoadInfo::Clone (after the new TRRLoadInfo); TRRLoadInfo::SetOriginAttributes (first statement)
inventory.notes: The TRR load info keeps the origin attributes of the lookup's context, so the proxy filters see it: Clone copies them to the new TRRLoadInfo, and SetOriginAttributes, which Mozilla answers with NS_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, stores them through StealthTRRSetOriginAttributes (a guard that returns its result). The Juggler load identifier accessors are in StealthLoadInfo.cpp, not in this file.

verifier.why: The infallible-stub risk is refuted: upstream TRRLoadInfo already does this for other infallible attributes.

inventory.notes: Exports StealthTRRContext.h and builds StealthTRRContext.cpp, the carrying of the DoH request's browser context to the proxy lookup it causes.

inventory.anchor: TLSTransportLayer::Init, the AddToSocket of the TLS layered over a tunnel
inventory.notes: The TLS layered over a tunnel (an HTTPS proxy, an HTTP/2 tunnel) was added to its socket with default origin attributes, so what that TLS asks for on its own (the OCSP request of its certificate) had already lost the context of the page. StealthTransportContext (StealthTRRContext.cpp) gives it the attributes of the socket transport that carries it, as a direct connection has.

verifier.why: Written from the diff against the tag.

inventory.anchor: include of StealthTRRContext.h; MaybeResolveProxyAndBeginConnect; ResolveProxy; OnProxyAvailable; BeginConnect (the connection info)
inventory.notes: The proxy lookup of a DoH request is made for the context of its load info, and fails closed: a lookup that fails or cannot start ends the request (StealthTRRProxyFailure) instead of going DIRECT, which would send the name from the host's own address. The connection info of the request carries the context's origin attributes, so a tunnel of one browser context (its proxy credentials) is never reused by another.

verifier.why: Written from the diff against the tag.

inventory.anchor: include of StealthTRRContext.h; nsHttpChannel::MaybeResolveProxyAndBeginConnect; nsHttpChannel::OnProxyAvailable
inventory.notes: A DoH request that runs as an nsHttpChannel (the main thread) fails closed like the TRRServiceChannel: when its proxy lookup fails or cannot start, the channel ends with StealthTRRProxyFailure instead of failing over to DIRECT (StealthFailClosedOnProxyFailure decides: a TRR channel, not cancelled, with a failed status). Other channels are untouched.

verifier.why: Written from the diff against the tag.

inventory.anchor: OCSPRequest::Run, where the origin attributes of the OCSP channel are chosen
inventory.notes: The OCSP request of a certificate is made with the system principal and keeps of the page's origin attributes only the first party domain and the private browsing id, so it left in the default user context: outside the proxy and the resolver of the page's browser context. StealthKeepRequestContext (StealthTRRContext.cpp) adds the userContextId, the one the proxy filter and the resolver answer by; the default context is unchanged.

verifier.why: Written from the diff against the tag.

inventory.anchor: include of StealthParentalControls.h; the nsParentalControlsService constructor
inventory.notes: The constructor takes the declared value (off) and returns before its first OS call, so the Windows parental controls provider is never asked; every reader (nsHttpHandler, the DoH heuristics, downloads, CanonicalBrowsingContext) goes through the service and sees the same value.

verifier.why: Written from the diff against the tag.

inventory.anchor: HashCompleter.complete and openChannel: the completion road of a page's context
inventory.notes: complete() hands a completion of a non-default context to the completer of that context (StealthHashCompleterContext.sys.mjs), and openChannel gives the channel that context's origin attributes: the gethash request leaves by the proxy and the resolver of the page's context, and contexts never share a request. The default context takes Mozilla's code unchanged.
